newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN SEMICON PAYS T$3 MLN BONUS FOR EACH STAFF.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN SEMICON PAYS T$3 MLN BONUS FOR EACH STAFF.

text.p: Taiwan microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing said on Friday its employees could start trading the 100 million shares issued to them during a recent bonus issue.
Taiwan Semicon's 1.427 billion new shares -- 1.327 billion for shareholders and 100 million for employees -- began trading on Friday, public relations manager Tseng Ching-hao told Reuters.
Based on Thursday's closing price of T$151, the firm's bonus issue of 100 million shares for its 5,100 employees totalled T$15.1 billion, or T$2.96 million for each employee.

Taiwan Semicon in June made a bonus issue of T$5 per share, paying 500 free shares for every 1,000 shares held. It made bonus issues of T$8 per share in 1994 and another T$8 per share in 1995, Tseng said.
At 0345 GMT or 15 minutes before the stock market's close on Friday, Taiwan Semicon's share price was up T$6 to T$157.
Analysts said the expected selling pressure from the huge 1.427 billion bonus issue already had been pre-empted by recent consolidation of the firm's share price.
"The profit-taking from the huge bonus issue has been reflected in the share's recent consolidation, and it's time for it to rise again," said independent analyst Michael Hung.
